issues.legal_issue: Compensation statutorily allocated to junior members of an impartible estate is not part of the holder’s Hindu undivided family wealth when the statutory allocation makes it their exclusive property.
material_facts: The estate was impartible, and under customary law the holder could deal with its income and corpus while junior members had no claim to either, apart from a right of succession in limited circumstances.

The governing statutory scheme treated the estate as joint-family property for the purpose of determining compensation and directed distribution of the balance among the holder and his legitimate sons as sharers.
The holder had no right to the compensation allocated to his sons and could not require them to reimburse him.
The wealth-tax assessment included compensation payable to the holder’s sons in the family’s net wealth; the appellate authorities excluded it, and the Revenue challenged that exclusion.
issues.conclusion: The compensation paid or payable to the sons was their absolute property and could not be included in computing the wealth of the holder or his Hindu undivided family; the appeals were dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 45 and 49 of the Madras Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act, 1948, as adopted in Andhra Pradesh, operate together to allocate compensation to the relevant sharers and recognize devolution of an entitled person’s interest. The statutory allocation effects a partition for the compensation, making the sons’ allocated amounts their exclusive property. A statutory fiction created for a particular purpose cannot be extended beyond that purpose. The Court referred, on the nature of the impartible estate, to Rajah Velugoti Kumara Krishna Yachendra Varu v. Sri Rajah Velugoti Sarvagna Kumara Krishna Yachendra Varu, V.T.S. Thyagasundaradoss Thevar v. V.T.S. Sevuga Pandia Thevar, and Commissioner of Expenditure Tax, A.P. v. S.R.Y. Sivarama Prasad Bahadur.

rule.if: revenue_wealth_tax_appeal and statutory_allocation_to_junior_members and compensation_is_recipients_exclusive_property and holder_has_no_right_to_recover_it

predicates.revenue_wealth_tax_appeal: The Revenue challenges in a wealth-tax proceeding the exclusion of compensation from the assessed family wealth.
predicates.statutory_allocation_to_junior_members: A statutory scheme allocates compensation directly among junior members as individual sharers.
predicates.compensation_is_recipients_exclusive_pro: The statutory allocation makes the compensation received or payable to those members their exclusive property.
predicates.holder_has_no_right_to_recover_it: The estate holder has no right to claim or recover the compensation allocated to those members.
predicates.compensation_excluded_from_holder_family: The compensation allocated to the junior members is excluded from the estate holder’s family wealth.

issues.definition: When the Revenue challenges an exclusion in a wealth-tax proceeding, and a statutory allocation gives junior members exclusive compensation that the holder cannot recover, that compensation is excluded from the holder’s family wealth.
